title: incident-bot: prioritize runbook-linked auto-diagnostics and SLO-toolkit helpers
author: Marisol Chen
description: Context: On-call teams rely heavily on runbooks surfaced by incident-bot when diagnosing SLO/alert-driven incidents. Previous auto-diagnostics ranked suggestions purely by evidence score which sometimes surfaced low-value items when a runbook existed. Motivation: surface and prioritize diagnostics with explicit runbook links and surface SLO context from slo-toolkit to improve triage time and reduce on-call churn. This PR implements a runbook-aware prioritizer and small SLO-toolkit helpers to attach SLO metadata to diagnostics. Summary of changes: added a runbook indexer and caching layer, a new prioritizer that boosts diagnostics with runbook links and SLO context, helper functions in slo-toolkit to return canonical SLO identifiers and severity hints, telemetry to break down ranking signals, and unit + e2e tests covering priority edge cases and fallback behavior. Rollout plan: feature gated behind incident-bot config flag (autodiag.prioritize_runbook = true), staged rollout in Dedicated -> Hosted beta, monitor new telemetry signals and oncall feedback for 2 weeks before enabling globally. Backwards compatibility: when no runbook or SLO context is present, behavior falls back to existing evidence-based ranking. CI/Test: added unit tests for prioritizer, e2e that simulates alert -> diagnostic generation -> runbook linking, and bumped integration test expectations. Related work: ENG-4821 (autodiag ranking revamp), ENG-4900 (runbook indexing pipeline).
commits_summary: feat(runbook): add runbook indexer and caching; feat(prioritizer): runbook-aware ranking + weight tuning; feat(slo-toolkit): expose SLO identifier and severity_hint helpers; perf: cache runbook lookups in memory; test: add unit and e2e coverage; docs: update runbook linking guide
